title: Securing Endpoints with Role‑Based Access
description: Use HttpSecurity to define who can access which URLs.

slides.title: Fine‑Grained Authorization 🎯
slides.content:
# Restrict Access by URL Pattern

You can configure security rules using `authorizeHttpRequests()`:
- `permitAll()` – accessible without authentication.
- `authenticated()` – only authenticated users.
- `hasRole("ROLE")` – users with given role.
- `hasAnyRole("ROLE1", "ROLE2")` – users with any of the roles.
- `denyAll()` – no access.

quizData.question: Which method would you use to allow unauthenticated access to a specific URL?
quizData.explanation: permitAll() grants access to everyone, even unauthenticated users.

slides.title: Configuring URL Security
Order Matters! 🔢
slides.content:
# Rules Are Evaluated in Order

More specific rules should come first. For example:

```java
.antMatchers("/api/admin/**").hasRole("ADMIN")
.antMatchers("/api/**").authenticated()
```

If `/api/admin/users` matches both, the first rule applies because it's more specific.

Always end with `.anyRequest().authenticated()` or a catch‑all rule.

slides.title: Using Path Variables 🛣️
slides.content: You can also secure endpoints based on path variables: `antMatchers("/api/users/{id}").access("@userSecurity.checkUserId(authentication,#id)")` – but that's more advanced (method security is easier).
